taxa_and_assays.MngA_entry_comparisons: MngA is one 658-residue EIIABC chain. MC4100 mngA deletion loses MG transport and pACS31 restores it; inverted membranes plus general PTS extracts and PEP form MG-P. This is not a purified three-protein reconstitution. Separate intact-cell uptake comparisons in MG-induced MC4100 reported weak reduction with glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller effect with trehalose, and no observed reduction with fructose, maltose, arabinose, gluconate, glycerate, 1-alpha-glucosylglycerol, 2-alpha-glucosylglycerate or 2-alpha-mannosylglycerol. The Discussion instead describes mannose and those three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 micromolar radiolabeled MG; the mannose weak-effect/no-significant-effect tension remains unresolved. These are uptake comparisons, not direct binding, a proven competitive mechanism or inhibition constants. Separately, 300 mM NaCl during growth did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by about 50%; this is an induction endpoint, distinct from the KM522 500 mM salt-protection experiment and from a direct catalytic salt effect. None of these whole-cell comparisons is attributed to the pACS31 inverted-membrane assay.

evidence.interpretation: In induced MC4100 uptake experiments, Results reports weak effects of glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller trehalose effect, and no effect for fructose and the named non-PTS comparators. Discussion describes mannose and the three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 μM radiolabeled MG. These statements must coexist, rather than being upgraded into a robust direct competitive-inhibition mechanism. The same Results also reports that 300 mM NaCl did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by approximately half; this differs from the later KM522 500 mM salt-protection test.

The study uses MC4100 loss/rescue and reporter systems; its reference describes 391 residues, paper-numbered P297S in JA176 and a near-terminal Tn5 insertion in JA177. pRM1 carries MC4100 sdaR in pBluescript. Positive autoregulation is inferred from reporter responses and loss of functional sdaR.
The current issuing reference is P37047 with 385 residues. The author dossier retains this mismatch, but it is not on either regulatory subject endpoint in the YAML/page/export claim.
His189 is an Active site feature. The original Modified residue feature is Tyr122, so the existing locator does not locate the claimed catalytic histidine.
The current assertion combines nucleoid location with variable oligomers but locates only SUBCELLULAR LOCATION. Oligomer support occurs in SUBUNIT.
